informative.title: Compute Hjorth descriptors
informative.summary: Returns mean signal power, mobility, and a frequency-spread descriptor from finite differences.
notes: The input is not centered internally. Remove the baseline beforehand when its contribution to power is not wanted.
Complexity here is a frequency-scale descriptor, not the dimensionless ratio of mobilities.

references.note: Introduces the time-domain descriptor framework; the discrete energy estimator and edge cases are defined here.

definitions.text: For a finite real vector x of length N, let e0 = sum(x^2), e1 = sum(diff(x)^2), and e2 = sum(diff(diff(x))^2), where powers are elementwise and diff takes consecutive forward differences. Do not center the signal, extend the boundaries, or join samples across missing data. Compute differences in floating point.
Return e0 / N, the mean-square power of the input, without a 2*pi factor. A finite singleton has activity equal to its squared value.
For N >= 2 and e0 > 0, return sqrt(e1/e0) * sampling_frequency/(2*pi). Otherwise return NaN.

For N >= 3, e0 > 0 and e1 > 0, return sqrt(abs(e2/e1 - e1/e0)) * sampling_frequency/(2*pi). Otherwise return NaN. The absolute value applies to the full difference of ratios, including when the difference is negative.

behavior.nan_handling: Validate inputs first. If any signal sample is NaN, return NaN for all three outputs; do not omit or interpolate missing samples. Infinite and complex inputs are invalid.
behavior.input_orientation: Row and column vectors describe the same sample sequence. All outputs are scalars.
behavior.insufficient_data: A finite singleton returns its squared value and two NaNs. A length-two signal has undefined complexity. An all-zero signal has zero activity and NaN mobility and complexity. A nonzero constant of length at least two has finite positive activity, zero mobility, and NaN complexity.
